In this position, the Career & Alumni Services Manager manages academic quality assurance and improvement processes, including setting standards for course preparation, assessment, and evaluation. The Career & Alumni Services Manager coordinates regular meetings with advisory committees, program instructors, and student representatives for ongoing discussion of quality improvement and manages the resolution process for academic issues with instructors, students, parents, and partners. This position manages disciplinary processes in collaboration with colleagues from academic and administrative departments and provides regular reports on results to senior leadership in the department. Using advanced technical expertise, teaching and coaching experience, and organizational objectives, the Career & Alumni Services Manager resolves complex visiting student career- and alumni-related program issues and needs assessment initiatives and works on the most complex visiting student program issues, where analysis of situations requires an in-depth evaluation and understanding of organizational strategies and business objectives.

Establishes evaluation criteria for measuring desired results and impact. Manages academic quality assurance and improvement processes, including setting standards for course preparation, assessment, and evaluation. Coordinates regular meetings with advisory committees, program instructors, and student representatives for ongoing discussion of quality improvement. Manages the resolution process for academic issues with instructors, students, parents, and partners. Manages disciplinary processes in collaboration with colleagues from academic and administrative departments. Provides regular reports on results to the department's senior leadership.

Evaluates prospective program partnerships and supports department leadership and other staff in the development of on-campus and global partnerships. Coordinates with partners in the management and operations of existing programs.

Plans and develops career development focused/coaching/alumni related programs and curriculum, and adjusts existing courses and curriculum working closely with the Berkeley Global Team, the Academic Policy Committee, and instructors to manage the planning and scheduling of course offerings. Plans and manages program-related events

Uses considerable discretion to determine methods and procedures for current and new course offerings and topics. Collaborates regularly with other program directors and managers in the department to ensure standardization across programs.

Recruits, selects, orients, evaluates, and supervises qualified accredited and/or certificate instructors. Works closely with program directors/managers, the Academic Policy Committee, and Berkeley Global leadership to ensure excellence in all areas of instruction and coaching across programs.
Develops and facilitates 1 non-credit career development workshop or course per academic semester, including curriculum design, classroom instruction, and student career mentorship.
Uses business software systems in the completion of work assignments (for example, Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint).

Proficiency in instructional and other technology such as LMS (Canvas), online video conferencing (Zoom), Microsoft Suite, Google Suite, file sharing (Dropbox), and other tools and/or comparable technological expertise.
Continuing education in a related field.
Possesses advanced analytical, problem-solving, interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills.

Demonstrates knowledge of campus policies and procedures in a higher education environment; advanced knowledge of functional areas and understands how work impacts other areas of public educational programs.

Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and cross-cultural communication skills sufficient to represent the university in meetings with leaders and senior-level representatives of other organizations
